MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 12, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell at
5:00 p.m., on December 12, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00
p.m. on December 7, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk
CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigations: People ex. rel. Schlesinger v. Sachs,
  et. al., OCSC No. 30-2022-01262431-CU-JR-CJC; and Schlesinger v. Mission Viejo, OCSC
  Case No. 30-2022-01253878-CU-WM-CJC.

  Randall Simmons, M.V.: Stated that there should be no more tax money spent on an appeal. Voiced
  concerns on the cost burden to the City. He asked that the Council reconsider retaining the City
  Attorney

  Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Voiced her reasons for the City to no appeal the Court of Appeals decision
  and to stop wasting any more money. She asked that the Council admit defeat, apologize and move
  on. Lastly, she suggested that it is time to replace Mr. Curley.

City Council Minutes  1  December 12, 2023
   Barbara Casserly, M.V.: Expressed concerns of the unprofessionalism of the City Attorney’s
  response in October at the plaintiff’s attorney. She stated there was a time when we could
  respectfully disagree and said that she didn’t speak out in the past because she didn’t want the
  organizations she represented harm because of her activism. She asked the amount spent on legal
  fees be disclosed to the public for transparency and that the City stop fighting this judgement and
  to consider hiring a new attorney.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that the City’s actions have been indefensible and outlined her
  reasons. She criticized the City Attorney on his comments to the public, handling of the cases and
  stated he should be fired immediately. She also suggested that City Manager Wilberg should step
  down and that Keith Rattay should not be the next City Manager. She emphasized that the City has
  two years of illegal votes without a quorum and is in legal jeopardy.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel-Potential Litigation: Significant exposure to litigation
  pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case)

CS3. Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay;
  City Attorney William Curley; and Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz: Employee
  Organization: Service Employees’ International Union (SEIU)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:12 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting the Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley stated as to CS1 that since 2018 the City has bee working in collaboration with
the plaintiff, SouthWest Voters Registration Project to advance minority voter rights and to further
define the contours of the California Voters Rights Act. He indicated that this as not bee litigated much
and that it is very unclear. Attorney Curly said we have succeeded in that, although not in the ultimate
way we had hoped. He said we are proud of our cutting-edge joint efforts with the plaintiffs and feel
that we have advanced the Voting Rights understanding for minority voters. By unanimous decision,
the council determined the outcome is suitable and it achieved in a way the goals that the Council had
set out. So no further litigation is needed, the matter is closed.

INVOCATION: Mayor Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. State of the City

  Received presentation.

City Council Minutes  2  December 12, 2023
 P2. Panam Sports General Assembly ~ Santiago, Chile

  Received presentation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked where is the City’s press release on the outcome of the Court of Appeals
decision. Raised concerns on the cost to taxpayers and stated that the City Attorney should be fired and
sued for malpractice. She thanked and congratulated the plaintiff’s attorney’s as well as Michael
Schlesinger for putting his name on the complaint.

Michelle O’Brien, M.V.: Thanked the Council and Staff for the beautiful holiday lights and Santa’s
Workshop. She thanked Mayor Goodell for his hard work this past year as well as the other Council
Members.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Congratulated the Mission Viejo Diablos Football Team on their state
championship win against De La Salle and highlighted the season.

Daniel Croft, M.V.: Introduced himself as the head of the Mission Viejo Girls Softball League and
thanked the City Council. He recognized employees, Corey Gonyea, Jerry Hill, Mark Nix, Brian Zahn,
and Barbara Swanson for all their hard work.

Lynn Holmes, M.V.: Spoke out against the City Attorney for giving bad advice and asked who or what
is keeping him as legal Counsel for the City. She stated the loss of millions of dollars due to legal fees
and court costs. She feels that he should resign if the Council is not strong enough to terminate him.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of the loss of millions of dollars to taxpayers and win or lose Mr.
Curley and the lawyers made a lot of money. Asked to hear the concern from the two newest Council
Members, past Council Member, and staff on what their voice is on this matter.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Stated that due to the Court of Appeals decision that Council Members
Bucknum, Goodell, and Kelley should be removed from office. He outlined his reasoning and asked that
the City Council direct the City Attorney to file suit against Bucknum, Raths, and Sachs to return the
salaries and benefits they earned during their illegal terms of office and to recover any legal fees the
City has expended defending them. Lastly, he demanded the City Manager to be fired for allowing the
City to get to this point and that Council Members Bucknum, Goodell, and Kelley to recuse themselves
from any discussions involving my Quo Warrant and Mandate Cases.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Thanked Mayor Goodell for his term as Mayor. He spoke on Stop the Monster
and his survey that he conducted and suggested that the City should conduct an appraisal and consider
buying this property to improve the Garden Plaza.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Spoke on the Quo Warranto and recapped the case. He spoke out against the City
Attorney and City Manager. Asked why the City Manager didn’t get a second opinion and blamed the
Council for not questioning the City Attorney. Voiced his opinion that the City Attorney should be
terminated. He stated that the City Council should vote to waive the attorney-client privilege on the cost
of attorney fees.
City Council Minutes  3  December 12, 2023
 Tom Moore, M.V.: Stated sadly that he agrees with most of what has been said this evening. He
commented on the Los Osos Project saying currently there is only a sliver of representation on the
commercial part of the project. He questioned the size of the “for lease” sign on the South East corner
of La Paz and Marguerite and asked if it is supposed to be there.

Helen Maurer, M.V.: Stated that the Council needs to face the music and apologize and take their
personal responsibility to make things right. She asked that the Council stop costing the taxpayers any
more money.

Chris Alva, M.V: Spoke on Mission Viejo Girls Softball League and thanked the City’s support for their
league.

Jeff McBride, M.V.: Raised concerns on Oso and Felipe and asked that the turn pocket be longer or
changing the signals. Spoke on the dirt hauling that is affecting traffic and asked when it is going to
end.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

NOES:  None

OLD BUSINESS
City Council Minutes  6  December 12, 2023
 22. LOS OSOS Phase I Collaborative Design Team Contracts

  Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Asked that this item be tabled and to not throw away any more taxpayer
  money. He indicated he would be in favor when the business owners show up and speak in favor
  of this project.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Voiced his concerns of favoritism and lack of competition to potential
  corruption. He read from an article dating back to August 2010 that he wrote on design services
  and the City Manager’s authority.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned if the purchase of the Stein Mart Building was legal and asked
  the status of the building. Asked for transparency on the RJM non-bid contract and asked that
  the City go out to bid on this project.

  Council Member Vasquez questioned why this project did not go out to bid and made a motion
  to require additional documentation that includes the breakdown of the contract to RJM and to
  come back at next months meeting after review of this documentation. Motion died for lack of
  second.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1) approve
  the contract with Carlson Strategic Land Solutions, Inc. (A23-61) for the Core Area Vision Plan
  CEQA and regulatory permitting and environmental studies for an amount not to exceed $78,800
  and issue a purchase order for $78,800; (2) approve the proposal with GMU Engineers &
  Geologists for the preparation of a soils report and pavement evaluation in an amount not to exceed
  $61,320 and issue a purchase order for $61,320; (3) approve the proposal with RJM Design Group
  in an amount not to exceed $459,500 and issue a purchase order for $459,500; and (4) the Assistant
  City Manager will provide the breakdown of the contract to the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

  Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to appoint Bob Ruesch
  to the Orange County Vector Control District for a two-year term from January 1, 2024 through
  December 31, 2025.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  7  December 12, 2023
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CITY MANAGER REPORTS

City Manager Wilberg highlighted that the Heroes and Helpers event that is sponsored by Orange
County Sheriff’s Department and Orange County Fire Authority was a success. This year, through
donations from staff and business partners in the community including the Nadadores they were able to
fund 29 students each of which was give two hundred dollars to purchase gifts for themselves and family
members at the Target on Jeronimo. He stated that similarly when he ran into Gail Wood, she was in the
process of driving down her eighth truckload of gifts to 195 Marine families at Camp Pendleton.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum attended the Winter Gala at the community center, Kurt Pringle’s Christmas
party at the Ranch Saloon Restaurant, and the Animal Services volunteer holiday party. Council Member
Bucknum also attended the Mission Viejo High School Football championship game at Saddleback
College and commented on how wonderful it was to see so many alumni and second generation playing
for the Diablos. She attended the Hanukkah Celebration and lighting of the menorah. She reminded
residents to come to the Mix and Mingle this Saturday at the Civic Center and the Night Market. She
thanked staff for this great event. She stated she attended last year and you don’t want to miss it. Council
Member Bucknum felt that today is hopefully an important closure on the protracted costly and what
has appeared based on many comments is politically motivated litigation over our elections and the
implementation of district-based voting. She stated that throughout this process we sought to defend
the integrity and stability of the electoral process following state and local election codes by minimizing
litigation expenses all while attempting to establish a voting system that ensures representation for the
diverse communities that make up our City. She commented that staff and former council members have
been falsely accused of criminal wrongdoing and attempts were made to go after personal assets, our
homes. She shared concerns on how this chills participation for future people who want to run for office.
She stated that while the City and its attorneys vigorously disagree with the current rulings in the cases
our primary focus now is moving forward and mitigation further litigation expenses. Council member
Bucknum emphasized that quality of life, infrastructure and city services are what matter most. She
stated she is very passionate about the quality of life and the regulation of sober living homes that we
are working on with other cities. She wished everyone a Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukkah,

Council Member Ruesch

City Council Minutes  8  December 12, 2023
 Council Member Ruesch stated he feels very privileged to be able to attend so many great events. H
highlighted that on the 29th of November he attended the ACCOC Regional Holiday Reception at
Strawberry Farms and had a fun time. He also attended the Winter Gala with fellow Council Members.
Today he presented to Palmia Residents the Los Osos video and the residents were very excited for this
project. Lastly, he showed pictures form the even this past Sunday at eh Oso Creek Golf Course Lunch
with Santa. He raved about the event and complimented staff and the chef for the delicious food that
was served.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated she attended the Santa’s Arrival and Tree Lighting event with her
family. This past weekend she attended the fentanyl even at the community center which was very
informative and was given little containers of Narcan. She learned how such a small quantity of fentanyl
can kill a person. Council Member Vasquez took her girls to Santa’s Workshop and her youngest was
able to deliver a letter to Santa and noted that she did receive a letter back from Santa and her daughter
was delighted. She also attended the Winter Gala and gave kudos to staff for the time and effort that
was put in this event. She also attended the Character Awards at Bathgate and stated the best way to
define “thankfulness” is what makes your heart happy and to think of those special times with family or
friends. Council Member Vasquez attend the mural unveiling at Viejo Elementary School which was
painted by an artist who is a member of the Daughters of the American Revolution. The artist painted
the mural to represent early California life as part of our American 250 birthday of our Country coming
in 2026. Lastly, she stated that her husband took the girls to the Oso Creek Express Train and she also
attended the Hanukkah event which had a really great turnout.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley missed a few of the events last week due to babysitting two of her granddaughters
for the week ages two and five. She was able to take the around to the library and the mall and Santa’s
arrival. She gave a shout-out to the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for all their hard work putting
this event on and hosting Santa’s Workshop several nights a week. She also attended the Hanukkah
event and stated it was a very nice celebration. Lastly, she wished everyone a very Happy Hanukkah,
Merry Christmas and noted that her family celebrates Christmas as the birth of Christ so it’s very special
to her family.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell mentioned that he also rode on Santa’s train with his granddaughter and had the privilege
to read T’was the Night Before Christmas at Santa’s Arrival. He stated that it has been a pleasure to
serve as the Mayor this past year and thanked his colleagues for allowing him this opportunity. Mayor
Goodell said it has been an exceptional year other than a few battles and negative things, but all in all
he feels the state of the city is really great and we have a lot to be thankful for. He looks forward to the
coming year working with his colleagues as they have a great deal of potential to fulfill to make our City
even better than it already is. He said it’s a privilege that we get to do what we do even though there are
challenges. He wished everyone a very Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukkah and Happy Kwanzaa and
reminded everybody that it’s the spirit of love we are celebrating.

25. Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem 2024
City Council Minutes  9  December 12, 2023
   Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum to appoint Trish Kelley
  to serve as Mayor in 2024.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to appoint Bob
  Ruesch to serve as Mayor in 2024.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to appoint Bob
  Ruesch to serve as Mayor in 2024.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:17 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 9, 2024, at 5:00 p.m.
